intended_object: The graded resolution theorem (Weibel's K-book, II.7.6). For a graded exact category C and a resolving subcategory P stable under the grading shift, inclusion induces an isomorphism K₀^gr(P) ≅ K₀^gr(C) of ℤ[q,q⁻¹]-modules, whose inverse is the Euler class of a finite P-resolution. Inferred from the docstring, the module doc and the companion lemmas.
explanation: The definition is the library's ungraded resolution equivalence, transported to the graded K₀ groups and upgraded to a ℤ[q,q⁻¹]-linear equivalence. The private lemma `resolutionAddEquiv_apply` shows that the forward map is the map induced by the graded inclusion of P, which gives the linearity; `laurentResolutionEquiv_toLinearMap` restates this publicly. `laurentResolutionEquiv_symm_of` shows that the inverse sends [X] to the alternating sum of any finite P-resolution. `IsResolving` imposes the standard conditions: P contains zero, is closed under binary products and extensions, contains the kernel term of a conflation whose other two terms lie in P, and gives every object a finite P-resolution. The condition `hshift` (P equals its inverse image under the shift) is exactly what makes the induced exact structure on P graded. The ambient hypotheses (preadditive, zero object, binary biproducts, essentially small) are the natural setting for exact categories and their K₀. Mathlib has no graded K₀ of exact categories and no resolution theorem, so nothing more general exists.
